title: Harden command journal failure evidence
summary: Implements verified command journal and Command History evidence trust fixes for route exceptions, persistence degradation visibility, and duplicate local failure display.
reason: The command journal close-readiness review found that route exceptions were not durable command evidence, journal persistence degradation was invisible, and repeated identical local-only failures could be collapsed in Command History.
behavior_before: Unexpected command route exceptions returned sanitized 500 responses without persisted command-result rows; non-strict JSON or SQLite journal persistence failures were log-only; repeated identical local Command History failures could be deduped into one row.
behavior_after: Unexpected command route exceptions are converted into sanitized desktop_command_result.v1 journal rows before the 500 response is sent; /api/commands includes journal_persistence metadata for JSON and SQLite mirror status; local Command History rows receive unique local identities so repeated identical local failures remain visible until matching backend evidence replaces them.

required_tests: route exception journal policy unit test
local API route exception command journal integration test
implementation_ledger.notes: POST route exceptions now record a sanitized local_api.route_exception command-result journal row when the route policy allows journaling; secret-transfer and explicitly unjournaled routes remain suppressed.

required_tests: JSON save failure persistence metadata test
SQLite mirror failure persistence metadata test
implementation_ledger.notes: CommandJournal tracks JSON save and SQLite mirror status and exposes journal_persistence metadata from /api/commands without weakening non-strict recording semantics.

required_tests: WebView command history local duplicate smoke test
implementation_ledger.notes: Command History local rows now carry unique local_id values; empty backend refreshes preserve repeated local failures, and matching backend evidence still replaces local-only rows.
